bull_bear.body: Prioritizing debt reduction in Hyderabad Metro (target: Rs.7.5-8T from Rs.13T over 24 months via Rs.3T govt interest-free loan and Rs.2-2.5T TOD monetization); divesting non-core assets (Nabha, L&T IDPL); maintaining strong balance sheet (CRAR 22.6%, net debt-equity 0.89); reinvesting in strategic growth areas (green tech, digital)
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Elevated inflation and input cost volatility; supply chain disruptions; global recession impacting IT spends; delayed state capex awards; currency depreciation; delays in divestments (Nabha, IDPL); margin slippage in fixed-price contracts; geopolitical instability in GCC
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on India/GCC growth tailwinds and order book visibility; cautiously optimistic on margin recovery in H2; transparent about headwinds (costs, supply chain); committed to capital efficiency and ROE improvement via divestments and restructuring; avoiding overpromising on guidance
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Hyderabad Metro's EBITDA margin of 39% is driven by operational efficiency, not revenue growth alone; ridership surge (441K/day) is a leading indicator for future cash flow stability; L&T's 85% variable-price infrastructure contracts provide natural inflation hedge; private sector order prospects up 10% YoY signals structural shift in India's capex dynamics
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Divestment of Nabha Power completed on 25-Jun-2026; SPA signed to divest LTMRHL stake to Hyderabad Metro Rail Ltd (Hyderabad Metro classified as Held for Sale).
- Gross Debt / Equity Ratio 1.01 and Net Debt / Equity Ratio 0.39 as at Jun-26 (0.95 and 0.35 at Mar-26).
- Group Cash & Cash Equivalents and Current Investments of ₹851 bn at Jun-26 vs ₹804 bn at Mar-26; Standalone ₹426 bn, LTM & LTTS ₹177 bn, L&T Finance ₹115 bn, Other Subsidiaries ₹133 bn.
- Deck attributes lower finance cost to a decline in average borrowings, and notes interest cost for Hyderabad Metro has not been considered from 01-May-2026.
- Net Working Capital improved to 4.9% of revenue as on Jun'26 from 10.1% as on Jun'25.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Infrastructure: order inflows Rs.251B (+107% YoY), order book Rs.2.6T, revenue Rs.194B (+39% YoY), EBITDA margin 6.6% (-170 bps YoY); Hydrocarbon & Power: order book Rs.689B, revenue Rs.55.9B (-7% YoY), EBITDA margin 8.5% (+190 bps YoY); Defense & Heavy Eng: order book Rs.197B, revenue Rs.14.6B (-1% YoY); IT&TS: revenue Rs.101.5B (+29% YoY), margins pressured by wage inflation; Financial Services: retail book 58%, improved NIM and asset quality; Development Projects: Hyderabad Metro ridership up to 441K/day (Oct), EBITDA margin 39% (vs 13% YoY), PAT loss reduced to Rs.3.28B; Other: buoyed by Smart World & Comms, Construction Equipment

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Order Book of ₹7,790 bn as on 30-Jun-2026 (₹6,128 bn as on 30-Jun-25); the deck states international orders constitute 52% of the Order Book.
- Order Book geography mix: India 48%, Middle East 37%, USA & Europe 8%, ROW 8%; segment mix: Infrastructure & Utilities 45%, Energy-Conventional 28%, Energy-Green 19%, Manufacturing & Products 5%, Services 2%.
- Deck claims a "strong addressable prospects pipeline of ~ Rs 15 trillion for the near term".
- Segment architecture spans Infrastructure & Utilities, Energy-Conventional, Energy-Green, Manufacturing & Products (together "Projects, Products & Manufacturing"), Technology Platforms & Services, Financial Services, Realty and Development Projects, plus new businesses (Green Hydrogen/Ammonia, Electrolyser Manufacturing, Semiconductor, Data Center, Digital Platforms).
- Q1 FY27 revenue composition: India 49% / Middle East 29% / USA & Europe 19% / ROW 3%; International Revenue stated at 51% of revenue.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [M&A] LTM issued an offer to acquire Randstad's Technology and Consulting Services business.
- [Credit rating] Moody's Ratings assigned a 'Baa1' long-term / Stable rating, which the deck describes as two notches above the Sovereign Rating.
- [Macro — India] Near term: private capex recovery broadening; resilient new capex areas in digital infra, energy transition and GCC-led real estate capex; fiscal slippage risk from subsidy outlays amid conflict; oil-driven inflation risk. Long term: strategic self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) in manufacturing and defence, and capital reallocation to data centers, EVs and advanced manufacturing.
- [Macro — Global] Tech capex supercycle in AI, cloud and data centers; supply chains being reworked; supply chain de-risking via friendshoring/nearshoring; technology as the new geopolitical battleground.
- [ROE caveat] The 16.1% ROE (TTM) is footnoted as including a 100 bps impact of a Labour Code provision recognised in Q3 FY26.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Projects & Manufacturing EBITDA margin down 80 bps YoY to 8.2% due to job mix, close-out costs (two projects), and legacy procurement at high commodity prices; cost pressures from energy, design changes, and delayed sourcing; margin recovery expected in H2 due to favorable new procurement and project milestones
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Group order inflows and revenue guidance of 12-15% (bias to upper end); Projects & Manufacturing EBITDA margin target of 9.5% for FY23, but at risk due to supply chain and input cost volatility; NWC-to-sales to end FY23 at ~20%
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.3.72T (record), 72% domestic, 28% international; 91% from Infrastructure & Energy; domestic breakdown: State Govt 30%, PSUs 42%, Central Govt 10%, Private 18%; international: 80% GCC, 10% Africa, 10% SEA
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Green hydrogen electrolyzers (pilot operational Nov'22, JV partner selection by Mar'23); Data Centers (Panvel pilot Jan'23, Kanchipuram by Mar'24); L&T EduTech and SuFin digital platforms live and performing; TOD monetization for Hyderabad Metro; potential InvIT in Metro post-2025
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: L&T is capitalizing on India's robust public and private capex cycle and GCC infrastructure spending, with strong order inflows and a record order book, while navigating margin headwinds from input costs and supply chain disruptions; its strategic pivot into green tech and digital services offers long-term growth optionality.
